input.description:
**Answered — safe to delete.**

Probe for awinogradov/code-assistants issue 501. Three cases were exercised on this ticket.

**1. Nested fence renders correctly.** With the description shaped like `linear:create` output and then wrapped, the outer section rendered collapsed as `▶ Original task`; expanding it revealed a nested, independently collapsible `▶ Original prompt` beside the rest of the body, with `## Implementation plan` outside at top level.

**2. Re-store is idempotent.** Replacing from the `## Implementation plan` anchor to the end left exactly one `Original task` wrapper, returned the preserved prefix byte-identical, and swapped only the plan.

**3. Empty description produces no wrapper.** Storing onto an empty description wrote the plan alone, with no empty collapsible.

**Bonus finding: Linear normalizes the fence on save.** Text written as `+++ Title … +++` is stored and returned as `>>> Title … >>>`. Both are accepted on input; `>>>` is canonical. Normalization happens once — an already-normalized prefix round-trips unchanged. Linear also rewrites `_italic_` to `*italic*` and `-` bullets to `*`. Anything grepping a fetched description for a literal `+++` will miss, which is why the stored-plan format anchors on the heading rather than the fence.

No behaviour change was needed. Findings recorded in that repository's chapters 16 and 11.

content.text:
That reviewer catch was fair and I ran the other two cases rather than deferring them. **All three of #501's cases are now observed:**

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Nested fence | Outer collapses as `▶ Original task`; inner `▶ Original prompt` nests inside and collapses independently |
| Re-store | Exactly one wrapper survives, prefix byte-identical, only the plan swapped |
| Empty description | Plan written alone, no empty collapsible |

The re-store case was the one most worth running, because of the finding that made it non-obvious: **Linear rewrites `+++ Title … +++` to `>>> Title … >>>` on save.** The wrapper on disk doesn't match what the skill writes, so had `linear:plan` detected a prior store by matching `+++`, every re-store would have read as a first store and stacked another wrapper each planning cycle. It survives only because it anchors on the `## Implementation plan` heading — now written down as a rule rather than left as an accident.

A related detail that makes the design work: normalization happens **once**. An already-`>>>` prefix round-trips byte-identically, which is what makes the "abort if the preserved prefix changed" safety check usable instead of a permanent false alarm.

Still to come, in order: **#503** (record passes-spent and exit reason so the 98-threshold sample accrues by itself) and the **turbo cache-input fix** you approved.
